# **Software Requirements Specification: Cross-Subsystem Semantic Transition, Surviving Reader Adaptation, and Sequenced Rollout Architecture**

## **1\. Operational Boundaries, System Assumptions, and Untouched Subsystems**

### **1.1 Architectural Context and the Semantic Seam**

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) governs the architectural seam and deployment sequence for transitioning a multi-certificate English exam-practice platform from a certificate-bound difficulty and band model to a unified, per-skill Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) measurement architecture1. Five core subsystems of the platform are undergoing clean-slate delete-and-rebuild replacements defined in sibling specifications: the unified content warehouse and analytical rubric specification1, the two-stage adaptive placement engine2, the sliding-window learning path and practice engine4, the high-contrast learner user interface5, and the staff authoring and governance workbench6.  
Concurrently, nine load-bearing subsystems survive this rebuild without being replaced from scratch, and every one of those surviving subsystems reads, stores, or acts upon a band, difficulty level, or capability record whose underlying mathematical meaning is changing3. In the legacy platform, a Band is a foreign-key reference or string code pointing to a row in a certificate's own native score table: TOEIC Listening and Reading (below\_A1 at 10–119 up to C1 at 945–990), IELTS Academic and General Training (B1 at 4.0–5.0 up to C2 at 8.5–9.0, stored as integers 40–90), VSTEP.3-5 (A2 through C1 stored as 40–100), TOEIC Multi-Stage Adaptive (CAT\_B1, CAT\_B2), and TOEIC Speaking and Writing (SW\_B1, SW\_B2)2. Conversely, the rebuilt placement and learning path engines operate on canonical CEFR levels (Pre-A1, A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2) paired with an intra-band position integer (![][image1]) per examined skill, alongside an overall CEFR level defined strictly as the weakest measured skill2.  
The central engineering hazard of this transition is semantic conflation across the seam between rebuilt writers and surviving readers3. A certificate band is not a CEFR level: the legacy platform internally labelled a combined TOEIC Listening and Reading score of 785–940 as "B2", which violates Educational Testing Service (ETS) standard-setting research showing that a candidate with 450 in Listening (B2) and 335 in Reading (B1) achieves a 785 total while remaining below the B2 threshold (385) in Reading1. Furthermore, two of the five certificates (TOEIC\_CAT and TOEIC\_SW) possess no CEFR-named bands in their native tables at all2. If surviving subsystems quietly alias certificate bands to CEFR levels, or if rebuilt writers ship out of phase with surviving readers, the platform will commit its worst possible failure mode: presenting a learner with two contradictory answers to the question of their current proficiency level on the same day3.

### **1.2 Settled Transition Invariants and System Assumptions**

Eight settled architectural decisions (Decisions T1–T8) and three environmental constraints anchor this specification3. Under Dual-Axis Separation (Decisions T1 and T2), CEFR (Pre-A1 through C2) serves as the exclusive scoring axis for placement, topic capability, and learning path scheduling, whereas native certificate scales remain the scoring axis for certificate mock exams and learner goal targets2. A certificate band is never silently equated to a CEFR level without an empirically defended per-skill standard-setting crosswalk1. Under Explicit Epistemic Honesty (Decision T3), wherever a certificate's band rows carry no defended CEFR mapping or no cumulative study-hour values, the system explicitly states cannot\_judge (CHƯA ĐỦ DỮ LIỆU ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỜ HỌC or "Không quy đổi tương đương CEFR") rather than fabricating an unverified level or study-hour estimate3.  
To prevent state corruption across concurrent workflows, Decision T4 mandates a single writer per derived fact: every derived snapshot in the database—specifically PlacementTests and PlacementSkillResults, ExamAttempts final band and score, LearnerSkillState, LearnerTopicCapability, and PathSteps closure—is mutated by exactly one deterministic service2. Simultaneously, Decision T5 enforces append-only financial auditability on the CreditLedger table, guaranteeing that historical ledger rows and their transaction\_reason codes are never deleted, mutated, or rewritten to tidy domain vocabulary3.  
Finally, Decisions T6, T7, and T8 establish a clean-slate cutover strategy over incremental patching3. Because the platform is pre-production, scheduled maintenance downtime is acceptable and starting clean is available at the lowest cost the product will ever encounter3. The environment contains no incremental database migration framework; the database schema is a single declarative SQL file (schema.sql) applied to a fresh database instance3. Old code paths are deleted immediately once their replacement passes verification rather than retained behind permanent feature flags3. Because code can be engineered in parallel whereas adaptive placement and levelled paths cannot function against the legacy 116-item bank, the rollout sequence in Section 5 and Section 8 enforces hard quantitative content gates—progressing from the 456-unit Demo Set to the 1,120-unit Minimum Viable Release (MVR) and the 2,120-unit Full Production Pool—before any learner-facing cutover occurs1.

## **2\. The Band-and-Level Semantic Map**

To prevent semantic drift across the five certificates (TOEIC\_LR, IELTS, VSTEP, TOEIC\_CAT, and TOEIC\_SW), the platform separates proficiency representation into two distinct data constructs that may only interact through an explicit, read-only projection boundary1. The first construct is the Canonical Skill CEFR Coordinate (SkillCefrCoordinate), a modality-specific measurement tuple ![][image3] where ![][image4], ![][image5] is the relative intra-band position, and ![][image6] with integer index ![][image7]2. Across the active examined skills ![][image8] of a certificate, the headline readiness floor is the non-compensatory minimum ![][image9]2. The second construct is the Native Certificate Band and Scaled Score (CertificateBandSnapshot), a certificate-specific performance record ![][image10] representing either a learner's score on a single mock exam paper or the learner's chosen target row in CertificateBands2.

## **3\. Numbered Functional Requirements for Surviving Subsystems**

### **3.1 Mock Exam Subsystem Requirements**

Evaluating whether the mock exam subsystem requires modification beyond band wording on its result page (Question 7\) requires analyzing every structural coupling between the mock exam sitting engine (ExamAttemptEngine) and the rebuilt warehouse, rubric, and path subsystems1. While the timed sitting viewport (SCR-EX-02), countdown timer expiry sweep, client-side draft synchronization, and one-way section locks remain intact2, four architectural adaptations are mandatory beyond result-page copy. First, whereas legacy mock exams pointed to static rows in the 116-item table (where the IELTS mock declared 40 items and held 2, and 5 of 13 sections held 0 items)1, mock exam blueprints must now bind to (item\_id, version) and (stimulus\_id, version) records in ObjectiveItems, ProductiveTasks, and StimulusGroups filtered by lifecycle\_status \= 'active' and content\_tier \= account.account\_mode, enforced prior to publication by the six-invariant Publish Readiness Rail (S-09 INV-1..INV-6)1. Second, on four-skill certificates (TOEIC\_LR, IELTS, VSTEP) and TOEIC\_SW, mock exam Speaking and Writing responses must be evaluated by the unified ![][image2] (0..6) analytical rubric (S\_FC..S\_GR, W\_TR..W\_GR) and projected onto the certificate's native scale using the piecewise linear interpolation formulas and task weights (![][image28] for IELTS and VSTEP) established in the content specification1. Third, to prevent a two-writer race condition between synchronous objective scoring and asynchronous AI free-response grading (Section 7.1, Defect 2), mock exam completion must be finalized exclusively by ExamAttemptScoringProjector once pending\_free\_response\_count \== 02. Fourth, every objective item and productive task answered inside a mock exam must feed CapabilityUpdateWriter (LearnerTopicCapability and LearnerItemExposure, per Decision L5) and emit a calibration comparison check against LearnerSkillState4.

#### **FR-MOCK-01: Native Scale Scoring and Per-Skill CEFR Equivalent Projection**

When a mock exam sitting completes (ExamAttempts.exam\_type IN ('full\_mock', 'mock\_section')), ExamAttemptScoringProjector SHALL compute both a native certificate score vector and a paper-specific per-skill CEFR equivalent (Question 1\)1. For the native certificate score vector, the projector computes each examined skill's raw and scaled score on the certificate's official scale (5–495 per skill and 10–990 sum for TOEIC\_LR and TOEIC\_CAT; 0–200 per skill with no combined sum for TOEIC\_SW; 0.0–9.0 in 0.5 steps for IELTS; and 0.0–10.0 in 0.5 steps for VSTEP) and resolves the matching row certificate\_band\_code from CertificateBands1. Simultaneously, for each examined skill ![][image12], the projector looks up the skill's scaled score against the defended per-skill standard-setting cut table (Tannenbaum and Wylie 2008 for TOEIC Listening, Reading, Speaking, and Writing1; Lim et al. 2013 for IELTS1; MOET Decision 729/QĐ-BGDĐT 2015 for VSTEP1) to record paper\_cefr\_equivalent. Under no circumstances may a combined multi-skill score (such as the 10–990 TOEIC total) be mapped to a single CEFR band1. For all TOEIC configurations and VSTEP.3-5, paper\_cefr\_equivalent caps at C1 (490–495 Listening, 455–495 Reading, 180–200 Speaking/Writing, 8.5–10.0 VSTEP) and never emits C21.

#### **FR-MOCK-02: Result Screen Disambiguation Between Paper Score and Profile CEFR**

On the Mock Exam Result Screen (SCR-EX-03), the user interface SHALL render two visually and structurally separated placards so a learner can never confuse a single paper's certificate score with their longitudinal CEFR standing (Question 1\)3. The primary placard ("KẾT QUẢ BÀI THI THỬ NÀY (THANG ĐIỂM CHỨNG CHỈ)") displays the paper's native overall scaled score, the native certificate\_band\_code sanitized via DisplayLabelRegistry (Rule COPY-01), and the per-skill native scaled scores alongside each skill's paper\_cefr\_equivalent badge labeled "Quy đổi bài thi này: \[CEFR\]"5. The secondary comparison placard ("HỒ SƠ NĂNG LỰC CEFR HIỆN TẠI CỦA BẠN") displays the learner's current per-skill discrete\_cefr · band\_position and weakest-skill overall\_cefr from LearnerSkillState, accompanied by an explicit explanatory notice whenever the paper's native overall band differs from overall\_cefr—explaining that the mock exam total combines skills using the certificate's compensatory sum or average rule (e.g., IELTS 6.5 or TOEIC 785), whereas the learning path's overall CEFR standing (e.g., A2) reflects the weakest measured skill (Speaking: A2 · 64\) to ensure no lagging modality is concealed1.

#### **FR-MOCK-03: Interaction Between Mock Exam Results and LearnerSkillState**

Completing a path-scheduled mock\_section calibration sitting SHALL directly update LearnerSkillState (discrete\_cefr, band\_position, continuous\_theta, last\_calibrated\_at) for that skill via SkillStateProjector and fire SKILL\_CEFR\_CHANGED (FR-REPLAN-01) whenever discrete\_cefr shifts4. Conversely, completing a standalone full mock exam (full\_mock) SHALL update LearnerTopicCapability and LearnerItemExposure for all attempted items and invoke CalibrationDetector (FR-CAL-01): if a skill's paper\_cefr\_equivalent on the full mock diverges from LearnerSkillState.discrete\_cefr, SCR-EX-03 SHALL render a one-click Calibration Confirmation Banner (Skill-Level-Shift-Replan-Notice5) allowing the learner to synchronize their LearnerSkillState and re-plan active weeks ![][image29] deliberately, rather than mutating their study plan silently4.

### **3.2 Exam Review Subsystem Requirements**

#### **FR-REV-01: Immutable Version Pinning and Defective-Item Notice in Review**

When rendering the per-question review screen for any completed attempt (ExamAttempts), the Exam Review query SHALL join AttemptItemResponses and FreeResponses directly to ObjectiveItems(item\_id, version), ProductiveTasks(task\_id, version), and StimulusGroups(stimulus\_id, version) with no filter on lifecycle\_status1. If an item or task version sat by the learner subsequently transitioned to lifecycle\_status \= 'retired\_defective', the review card SHALL render the exact historical stimulus, stem, options, and explanation sat during the attempt, topped by a Sign Gold (\#f2b705) transparency banner stating: "Câu hỏi này đã được thu hồi sau kỳ thi do lỗi kỹ thuật đáp án — điểm của bạn đã được bảo lưu hoặc cộng bù theo nguyên tắc có lợi cho người học"1.

#### **FR-REV-02: Post-Submission Item CEFR Badge and Evidence Span Highlighting**

For all attempts sat under the rebuilt model (scoring\_model\_version \= 'cefr\_v2'), each reviewed item card SHALL display the child item's canonical item\_level badge (\[ĐỘ KHÓ CÂU HỎI: A1..C2\]), its canonical topic title (R-INF · Suy luận hàm ý & Logic đoạn văn per Rule COPY-01), the distractor rationale for the learner's selected option, and the highlighted evidence\_span (char\_start..char\_end in the reading passage pane or start\_sec..end\_sec jump-to-audio button in the listening transcript)1.

#### **FR-REV-03: Rendering Pre-Rebuild Attempts Recorded Under the Old Level Model**

For any historical mock exam attempt preserved from prior to the transition cutover (scoring\_model\_version \= 'legacy\_v1'), the Exam Review screen SHALL render without error and enforce strict historical epoch isolation (Question 8\)3. The attempt's recorded certificate\_band\_code and scaled\_score SHALL render as a read-only Historical Certificate Scale Snapshot accompanied by an explicit badge ("Bản ghi lịch sử (Thang điểm chứng chỉ trước khi áp dụng chuẩn CEFR đa kỹ năng)"), and the system SHALL NOT retroactively fabricate a four-skill CEFR vector or 0–100 band\_position for a legacy\_v1 attempt3. Because DifficultyLevel 1–5 integers were uncalibrated and have no valid mapping to CEFR (Decision D2 and Decision T2), the review card for a legacy\_v1 attempt SHALL suppress the item difficulty badge entirely rather than printing "Level 3" or inventing a synthetic CEFR tag2. Finally, historical legacy\_v1 attempts remain viewable in the learner's past exam history list (SCR-EX-01), but are never ingested into LearnerSkillState, LearnerTopicCapability, or CalibrationDetector3.

### **3.3 AI Diagnostic Narrative Subsystem Requirements**

#### **FR-INS-01: Multi-Skill CEFR Prompt Context Schema**

Whenever the AiInsight subsystem constructs a prompt for a practice session (SCR-PRAC-04/05), placement result (SCR-PL-04), mock exam result (SCR-EX-03), learning path overview (SCR-LP-01), or dashboard (SCR-DB-01), the prompt builder SHALL pass a deterministic, schema-validated JSON payload (InsightContextPayload v2.0) that replaces the legacy single-band string (Question 5\)2. The certificate\_context object specifies certificate\_code, certificate\_display\_name, the examined\_skills array (\[L, R\] for TOEIC\_CAT; \[S, W\] for TOEIC\_SW; \[L, R, S, W\] for TOEIC\_LR, IELTS, VSTEP), and has\_cefr\_named\_bands (false for TOEIC\_CAT and TOEIC\_SW, true otherwise), stripping any skill where is\_examined\_by\_certificate \= false prior to serialization so the language model is blind to unexamined skills2. The overall\_standing object passes overall\_cefr (Pre-A1..C2 or null), overall\_band\_position (0–100), limiting\_skill (the specific skill that set the weakest-skill floor), and is\_partial\_result (boolean)2. The skill\_standings\[\] array provides for each examined skill its skill\_status (measured, reused\_from\_prior, grading, not\_measured), cefr\_level, band\_position formatted as "B2 · 71", intra\_band\_tier\_label ("Đầu bậc" for 0–33, "Giữa bậc" for 34–66, "Cuối bậc — sát ngưỡng lên bậc tiếp theo" for 67–100), projected\_certificate\_score\_range, estimated\_from\_single\_task (boolean), and—for Speaking and Writing—criterion\_profile (c1..c4 scores on 0..6, weakest\_criterion, and priority\_fix)1. Finally, goal\_context and event\_context supply target\_band\_display (sanitized via DisplayLabelRegistry), per\_skill\_target\_cefr\_floor, target\_exam\_date, weekly\_target\_hours, remaining\_guided\_hours, feasibility\_verdict, and pre-classified session capability deltas (direction: "gain" \| "hold" \| "drop" and crossed\_band\_boundary: boolean)4.

#### **FR-INS-02: Seven Prohibitions in AI Narrative Generation**

Because generative AI narrates stored deterministic facts and never chooses content, scores, or schedules, both the system prompt and a deterministic post-generation validator (InsightOutputGuardrail) SHALL enforce seven hard prohibitions on every generated narrative (Question 6\)2. The table below specifies each prohibition, the structural regex or schema check enforced by InsightOutputGuardrail, and the domain defect prevented.

| Prohibition ID | Prohibited AI Narrative Behavior (Answering Q6) | Deterministic Guardrail Check (InsightOutputGuardrail) | Domain & Psychometric Defect Prevented |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **PROHIB-INS-01** | **Synthetic Averaging of Skill Levels:** Averaging the four per-skill CEFR levels or contradicting overall\_standing.overall\_cefr. | Verifies that any mention of overall standing matches overall\_cefr and names limiting\_skill as the floor determinant2. | Prevents concealing asymmetric profiles (e.g., claiming a reader at B2 and speaker at A2 has an overall B1 readiness)2. |
| **PROHIB-INS-02** | **Percentage Formatting on band\_position or Cross-Band Regression Misreading:** Appending % to band\_position ("71%") or describing B2 · 82 \-\> C1 · 14 as a numerical drop. | Rejects regex \\b\\d{1,3}% attached to band position tokens; enforces promotion framing when crossed\_band\_boundary \= true2. | Eliminates the vertical-scale reset illusion where advancing into the bottom of a higher band reads as a score collapse2. |
| **PROHIB-INS-03** | **Fabricated Crosswalks on Non-CEFR Certificates or Unmeasured Skills:** Claiming CAT\_B2 or SW\_B2 equals "CEFR B2", or guessing a level/hour figure when not\_measured or cannot\_judge. | When has\_cefr\_named\_bands \= false, blocks strings equating CAT\_\* / SW\_\* to CEFR; enforces explicit unavailability phrasing2. | Enforces Decisions T2 and T3 across AI prose so non-CEFR certificates never hallucinate CEFR equivalence3. |
| **PROHIB-INS-04** | **Autonomous Content, Score, or Schedule Prescription:** Inventing a study schedule, promising item counts in future weeks, or assigning an unrecorded band score. | Restricts action references strictly to the single next\_step\_coordinate passed in event\_context3. | Preserves the core invariant that AI narrates deterministic state and never acts as planner or scorer2. |
| **PROHIB-INS-05** | **Raw Database Enum Key Leakage (Rule COPY-01):** Printing internal identifiers containing underscores or bare topic codes (L-INF). | Scans output for \[a-zA-Z0-9\]+\_\[a-zA-Z0-9\_\]+ (below\_A1, CAT\_B1, cannot\_judge, not\_measured, expanded\_remedial) and replaces via DisplayLabelRegistry5. | Prevents internal database vocabulary from reaching the learner's eyes5. |
| **PROHIB-INS-06** | **Praise, Flattery, Consolation, or Guessing Accusations (Rule COPY-02):** Using coaching clichés or accusing the learner of random guessing when non\_monotonic\_flag \= true. | Rejects banned phrase list ("Chúc mừng", "Tuyệt vời", "Bạn làm tốt lắm", "Đừng nản lòng", "Cố lên", "đoán mò")2. | Maintains the platform's objective signboard tone and protects learner trust in the instrument2. |
| **PROHIB-INS-07** | **Mutation of Domain State Tables:** Writing to any attempt, placement, capability, or path table during insight generation. | Database role for AiInsightWorker holds INSERT/UPDATE privileges solely on AiInsights (SELECT-only on all other tables)3. | Prevents AiInsight from acting as a competing second writer on any domain fact3. |

#### **FR-INS-03: Two-Stage Rendering and Broken-Stream Resilience**

On productive practice (SCR-PRAC-05), placement (SCR-PL-04), and mock result (SCR-EX-03) screens, deterministic scores and structured JSON rubric tables (c1..c4 tagged \[ĐIỂM DO AI ƯỚC TÍNH\] per Decision U12) SHALL render immediately in Stage 1 without waiting for AiInsight prose generation (Decision U1)5. AiInsight prose SHALL stream progressively in Stage 2 with a monospace block cursor (█, Decision U3) and display its exact generation timestamp (Decision U9)5. If the stream drops mid-generation (is\_complete \= false), the user interface SHALL retain the partial text, append \[CHƯA HOÀN CHỈNH\], and expose a zero-cost TẢI LẠI NHẬN XÉT retry action (Decision U4)5.

### **3.4 Weakness Analysis Subsystem Requirements**

Evaluating whether Weakness Analysis must change when items carry CEFR levels rather than 1–5 integers (Question 9\) reveals a critical psychometric constraint: flat aggregation by topic and exam section without conditioning on cefr\_level is no longer sufficient and generates severe diagnostic distortion1. Because the rebuilt warehouse crosses 20 canonical topics (L-GIST..W-DISC) orthogonally with 6 CEFR bands (A1..C2)1, summing a learner's historical responses on R-INF (*Bridging Inference*) across A2, B1, and B2 into a single unstratified topic percentage conflates stimulus difficulty with cognitive mastery: a B2 learner who missed stretch C1 inference items would see their R-INF accuracy drop below 50%, whereas an A2 learner who answered 10 of 10 A1 inference items and 0 of 5 B1 items would appear to hold 67% topic accuracy.

#### **FR-WEAK-01: Primary Level-Conditioned Topic Capability Aggregation**

The Weakness Analysis subsystem SHALL read directly from LearnerTopicCapability (written exclusively by CapabilityUpdateWriter, Decision L54) rather than executing a competing raw COUNT(\*) query over AttemptItemResponses3. For each examined skill ![][image30], Weakness Analysis SHALL anchor its primary diagnostic matrix at the learner's current skill CEFR level ![][image31] and classify the skill's canonical topics (6 in Listening, 6 in Reading, 4 in Speaking, 4 in Writing) into four ordered diagnostic tiers: Escalated Weak Spots (is\_weak\_spot \= true, where a repeated step failed to improve for the second consecutive time per Decision E2); Low Mastery (mastery\_band \= 'low', where recency-weighted Beta-Binomial mastery\_probability ![][image32]); Developing (mastery\_band \= 'developing', where ![][image33]); and Mastered at Current Band (mastery\_band \= 'mastered', where observations\_count ![][image34] objective items or ![][image35] productive tasks and ![][image36]), displaying any unlocked ![][image15] stretch cell (![][image37]) status alongside1.

#### **FR-WEAK-02: Productive Criterion Profile Integration**

Because Speaking and Writing tasks integrate multiple linguistic dimensions simultaneously across four genre topics (S-DESC..S-SYN, W-CORR..W-DISC), Weakness Analysis for productive skills SHALL pair the four topic capability cells at ![][image38] with the four analytical rubric criteria stored in LearnerSkillState.criterion\_profile (S\_FC, S\_PR, S\_LR, S\_GR for Speaking; W\_TR, W\_CC, W\_LR, W\_GR for Writing), explicitly flagging weakest\_criterion and its quoted evidence defect pattern1.

#### **FR-WEAK-03: Secondary Certificate Exam-Section Breakdown for Mock Exams**

To preserve section-level diagnostic utility for formal exam preparation (such as TOEIC Listening Part 3 or IELTS Reading Passage 2), Weakness Analysis SHALL maintain a secondary Mock Exam Section Breakdown view (section\_id) computed over completed ExamAttempts (exam\_type IN ('full\_mock', 'mock\_section')) for the active certificate\_code, displaying section accuracy alongside the mean item\_level (A1..C2) of items encountered in that section3.

### **3.6 Calibration Subsystem Requirements**

Evaluating what Calibration compares when placement outputs CEFR and practice accuracy is a percentage (Question 4\) demonstrates why level-conditioning is essential3. Comparing an unstratified percentage of correct practice answers against a CEFR placement level is meaningless because practice items span A1 to C21. However, when practice and mock item responses are conditioned strictly on item\_level \== LearnerSkillState\[s\].discrete\_cefr (![][image38]), the comparison becomes a direct binomial test of the Placement SRS's ![][image124] band mastery invariant (Decision D142) and the Content SRS's Binomial SPRT criterion (![][image125] non-mastery versus ![][image126] mastery under a ![][image127] guessing floor1).

#### **FR-CAL-01: Level-Conditioned Empirical Accuracy Comparison**

CalibrationDetector SHALL evaluate each examined skill ![][image12] after every completed step or mock sitting over a rolling window of unseen attempts (times\_seen \== 1 at the moment of attempt) recorded since LearnerSkillState\[s\].last\_calibrated\_at2. An Upward Calibration Trigger (UNDER\_PLACED\_SIGNAL) fires in skill ![][image12] currently at ![][image128] when the learner has completed ![][image25] unseen objective items at item\_level ![][image129] spanning ![][image35] canonical topics with cumulative accuracy ![][image130] AND completed ![][image131] unseen stretch items at item\_level ![][image132] with accuracy ![][image133] (or, for Speaking and Writing, completed ![][image134] tasks \[![][image135], Content SRS §5.3\] with composite rubric mean ![][image136])1. Conversely, a Downward Calibration Trigger (OVER\_PLACED\_SIGNAL) fires in skill ![][image12] currently at ![][image137] when the learner has completed ![][image25] unseen objective items at item\_level ![][image129] spanning ![][image35] canonical topics with cumulative accuracy ![][image138] (below the ![][image125] non-mastery boundary) OR has accumulated ![][image139] topics with is\_weak\_spot \= true (failed E2 repeat steps) at level ![][image38] (or, for Speaking and Writing, completed ![][image134] tasks at ![][image38] with composite rubric mean ![][image140])1.

#### **FR-CAL-02: Non-Accusatory Signboard Copy and Calibration Resolution**

When CalibrationDetector fires, the system SHALL NEVER accuse the learner of guessing on placement, claim the placement test was flawed, or silently alter their level without consent (Question 4\)2. Adhering to Rule COPY-02 (*Signboard, Not Coach*5), the user interface SHALL display a neutral Calibration Proposal Card on SCR-LP-01 and SCR-DB-01. For an upward signal, the card states: "Dữ liệu \[N\] câu luyện tập gần nhất ở kỹ năng \[Tên kỹ năng\] (Bậc \[L\_s\]) đạt độ chính xác \[X\]% trên \[K\] chủ điểm và \[Y\]% ở Bậc \[L\_s \+ 1\]. Hệ thống đề xuất điều chỉnh mức năng lực kỹ năng \[Tên kỹ năng\] lên Bậc \[L\_s \+ 1\] · 15 để lộ trình sát với thực tế." For a downward signal, the card states: "Độ chính xác trung bình qua \[N\] câu luyện tập kỹ năng \[Tên kỹ năng\] ở Bậc \[L\_s\] hiện đạt \[X\]%. Hệ thống đề xuất điều chỉnh mức luyện tập kỹ năng \[Tên kỹ năng\] về Bậc \[L\_s \- 1\] · 75 để củng cố nền tảng trước khi quay lại Bậc \[L\_s\]." The card provides two explicit actions: \[ĐIỀU CHỈNH LỘ TRÌNH NGAY\], which invokes SkillStateProjector to update LearnerSkillState\[s\], sets last\_calibrated\_at \= NOW(), and fires SKILL\_CEFR\_CHANGED (FR-REPLAN-01) to regenerate unstarted steps in ![][image29]; and \[GIỮ NGUYÊN MỨC HIỆN TẠI\], which snoozes calibration proposals for skill ![][image12] for 14 days and 30 additional items4.

### **3.7 Credit Ledger, Mentor Booking, and Saved Questions Requirements**

#### **FR-LEDG-01: Append-Only Immutability and Zero-Cost Action Enforcement**

The CreditLedger table SHALL prohibit UPDATE and DELETE operations via a PostgreSQL trigger (prevent\_ledger\_mutation()) in accordance with Decision T53. All historical ledger rows and transaction\_reason strings remain permanently readable as recorded3. LedgerTransactionWriter SHALL reject any attempt to insert a debit row (amount \< 0\) where source\_action\_type is placement\_sitting, placement\_ai\_grading, path\_step\_practice, path\_step\_ai\_grading, free\_drill\_session, free\_drill\_ai\_grading, or ai\_grading\_failure\_retry (BR-AI-02)2. Paid debits are restricted strictly to mock\_exam\_sitting and standalone\_paid\_ai\_eval3.

#### **FR-MENT-01: Structured Multi-Skill Mentor Booking Payload**

When a learner books a session with a mentor, MentorBookingService SHALL populate MentorBookings.learner\_standing\_snapshot (JSONB) from LearnerSkillState, LearningPaths, and ExamAttempts2. The payload SHALL include certificate\_code and sanitized target\_band\_display, overall\_cefr paired with overall\_band\_position and limiting\_skill, the per-skill cefr\_level · band\_position vector for all examined skills (with unexamined skills on TOEIC\_CAT and TOEIC\_SW explicitly marked is\_examined: false), the Speaking and Writing criterion\_profile (c1..c4 and weakest\_criterion), the list of is\_weak\_spot \= true topics, and the learner's most recent Mock Exam scaled\_score and certificate\_band\_code (if taken within 90 days) explicitly labelled as "Điểm thi thử gần nhất" alongside "Năng lực CEFR hiện tại"2.

#### **FR-SAVE-01: Saved Question Version Pinning, Stimulus Resolution, and Level Adaptation**

Transitioning the item bank from the legacy 116-item table (DifficultyLevel 1–5) to the unified warehouse (A1..C2) breaks saved questions in three ways unless remediated (Question 10): foreign keys pointing to purged legacy items fail, child items bookmarked without their parent passage or audio render as orphaned stems, and legacy 1–5 difficulty filters become dead controls1. To prevent all three failures, SavedQuestionsService SHALL enforce composite version pinning where SavedQuestions references (item\_id, pinned\_version) in ObjectiveItems (or (task\_id, pinned\_version) in ProductiveTasks) and automatically joins to the parent StimulusGroups(stimulus\_id, version) record so every bookmarked reading or listening question renders with its complete passage or audio player and evidence\_span highlight1. Furthermore, the Saved Questions view SHALL replace legacy 1–5 difficulty filters and certificate-locked section filters with filters for skill (Listening, Reading, Speaking, Writing), canonical topic\_id (L-GIST..W-DISC with Vietnamese titles per Rule COPY-01), and item\_level (A1..C2)1. Because SavedQuestions joins without filtering on lifecycle\_status, a bookmarked item that is later retired remains viewable; if lifecycle\_status \= 'retired\_defective', the card displays a Sign Gold notice ("Câu hỏi này đã được cập nhật phiên bản mới do lỗi kỹ thuật ở bản cũ") with a one-click button to re-pin the bookmark to the active version \= v \+ 1 replacement if one exists1.

## **4\. Business Rules for Semantic Reconciliation**

The eight business rules below govern how the platform reconciles numbers across the semantic boundary, what it displays when a certificate cannot produce a level, and how it handles pre-rebuild records1.

| Rule ID | Rule Name | Deterministic Specification & Learner-Facing Copy |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-SEM-01** | **Non-Equivalence of Single-Paper Mock Scores and Profile CEFR** | A Mock Exam result measures performance on **one test paper** scored on the certificate's native scale (using compensatory summing on TOEIC L\&R or 4-skill averaging on IELTS/VSTEP), whereas Placement and Path CEFR measure longitudinal **per-skill mastery** (![][image124] at band ![][image141] and all lower bands) where overall\_cefr is the **weakest examined skill**1. When the two numbers appear on the same screen (SCR-EX-03, SCR-DB-01, MentorBooking), they MUST carry distinct domain headers: "ĐIỂM BÀI THI THỬ (THANG CHỨNG CHỈ)" vs. "BẬC NĂNG LỰC CEFR HIỆN TẠI (THEO KỸ NĂNG YẾU NHẤT)"3. |
| **BR-SEM-02** | **Prohibition of Total-Score CEFR Crosswalks & Enforcement of C1 Ceilings** | No subsystem may ever map a combined TOEIC Listening & Reading total score (10–990, such as 785–940) to a CEFR level1. All CEFR projections from certificate scores MUST execute **per skill** against official minimum cut scores: TOEIC Listening (A1: 60, A2: 110, B1: 275, B2: 400, C1: 490), TOEIC Reading (A1: 60, A2: 115, B1: 275, B2: 385, C1: 455), TOEIC Speaking (A1: 50, A2: 90, B1: 120, B2: 160, C1: 180), TOEIC Writing (A1: 30, A2: 70, B1: 120, B2: 150, C1: 180), IELTS (B1: 4.0, B2: 5.5, C1: 7.0, C2: 8.5), and VSTEP.3-5 (B1: 4.0, B2: 6.0, C1: 8.5)1. Because TOEIC (all configurations) and VSTEP.3-5 do not measure C2, their native projections cap at C1 (495, 200, and 10.0), and a learner placed at C2 on those certificates sees "C2 (Vượt trần đo lường C1 của chứng chỉ — tương đương mức tối đa 495 / 200 / 10.0)"1. |
| **BR-SEM-03** | **Honest Representation on Non-CEFR Certificates (TOEIC\_CAT & TOEIC\_SW — Answering Q3)** | TOEIC\_CAT (CAT\_B1, CAT\_B2) and TOEIC\_SW (SW\_B1, SW\_B2) have no CEFR-named bands in their certificate tables (Decision T3)3. Their display behavior across all four learner states is governed deterministically by the **Non-CEFR Certificate Display Matrix** in Section 4.1 below2. |
| **BR-SEM-04** | **Asymmetric Profile vs. Target Band Comparison** | When a learner has a jagged per-skill profile (e.g., Listening B2 · 71, Reading B2 · 42, Writing B1 · 50, Speaking A2 · 64\) and targets a B2 certificate band, the system MUST NOT tell the learner they are "0% of the way to B2" simply because overall\_cefr is A22. Instead, SCR-PL-04, SCR-DB-01, and SCR-LP-01 plot all four skills against the vertical MỤC TIÊU: B2 line, explicitly marking Listening as \[ĐÃ ĐẠT MỤC TIÊU\] and identifying Speaking (A2 · 64\) as the KỸ NĂNG GIỚI HẠN requiring 52% of weekly study time4. |
| **BR-SEM-05** | **Cross-Band Promotion Formatting Rule (B2 · 78 \-\> C1 · 12\)** | Across all surviving and rebuilt readers, band\_position (![][image1]) is an intra-band coordinate on the 6-segment global horizon track, never a percentage2. Whenever a skill's ![][image39] increases across a band cut point (e.g., ![][image142], moving from B2 · 78 to C1 · 12), the delta badge MUST render in Sign Green (\#0a6b3c) as \[TĂNG BẬC: B2 (78/100) → C1 (12/100)\], never comparing ![][image143]2. |
| **BR-SEM-06** | **Unmeasured vs. Low-Proficiency Visual Separation (U11)** | If a skill is not\_measured (because both productive tasks failed AI grading under D7/D17, or the learner skipped the section) or is\_examined\_by\_certificate \= false, every reader MUST render CHƯA ĐO ĐƯỢC in neutral gray (\#575B5F) and exclude it from overall\_cefr, never rendering it as Pre-A1, 0, or error red (\#b31217), which is reserved exclusively for low measured proficiency2. |
| **BR-SEM-07** | **90-Day Cross-Certificate Skill Reuse and Expiry (D18, BR-DECAY-03)** | A measured skill result in PlacementSkillResults or LearnerSkillState remains valid for **90 calendar days** (expires\_at \= measured\_at \+ INTERVAL '90 days') across all certificates that examine that skill2. Switching from TOEIC\_CAT (L, R) to IELTS (L, R, S, W) within 90 days reuses L and R (skill\_status \= 'reused\_from\_prior', preserving original measured\_at) and tests only S and W2. |
| **BR-SEM-08** | **Historical Epoch Quarantine (legacy\_v1 vs. cefr\_v2)** | Any record preserved from before the Phase 4 cutover carries scoring\_model\_version \= 'legacy\_v1'3. legacy\_v1 records are strictly read-only historical artefacts: they render their original native certificate score/band with a historical epoch label, never undergo fake conversion to CEFR, and never feed LearnerSkillState, LearnerTopicCapability, Calibration, or LearningPaths3. |

### **4.1 Honest Display Specification for the Two Non-CEFR Certificates**

Question 3 requires designing the exact, honest answer shown for a learner on TOEIC Multi-Stage Adaptive (CAT) (CAT\_B1, CAT\_B2) and TOEIC Speaking & Writing (SW\_B1, SW\_B2) across every possible placement and history state, including when there is no answer3.

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **State 1: Learner Has Completed Placement on This Certificate** | Displays canonical CEFR \+ position for the **2 examined skills** (e.g., on TOEIC\_CAT: Nghe: B2 · 64, Đọc: B1 · 82; Bậc CEFR tổng quát (Kỹ năng yếu hơn): B1 · 82\) alongside the per-skill ETS scaled score projection (Nghe: \~430/495, Đọc: \~365/495)1. Explicitly states: *"Đánh giá đầu vào đo theo chuẩn CEFR (A1–C2). Chứng chỉ TOEIC Adaptive chia nhóm mục tiêu theo mã riêng (Mức B1 / Mức B2 Adaptive), không phải thang CEFR 6 bậc."* | Displays the learner's chosen target band via DisplayLabelRegistry (B1 (TOEIC ADAPTIVE) or B2 (TOEIC NÓI & VIẾT))5. Because CertificateBands.cumulative\_study\_hours is NULL on CAT\_\* and SW\_\*, displays CHƯA ĐỦ DỮ LIỆU ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỜ HỌC (cannot\_judge, Decision T3) unless the admin has populated defended 2-skill ETS cut hours (OQ-TR-02)2. | Completely hidden from SCR-PL-04, SCR-DB-01, SCR-LP-01, and AiInsight (is\_examined\_by\_certificate \= false, Decision D4)2. Sidebar links to /speaking and /writing redirect to /practice when on TOEIC\_CAT (SCR-PRAC-02/03)5. |
| **State 2: Learner Switched from TOEIC\_CAT to TOEIC\_SW (0 Valid Examined Skills Measured)** | Because TOEIC\_CAT measured L and R while TOEIC\_SW examines only S and W, **zero examined skills for TOEIC\_SW have a measurement**. The system honestly displays: "CHƯA CÓ DỮ LIỆU ĐÁNH GIÁ CHO KỸ NĂNG NÓI & VIẾT" (overall\_cefr \= NULL) while noting that Nghe (B2 · 64\) and Đọc (B1 · 82\) are stored safely in the learner's account for 90 days2. ## **5\. The Transition Sequence and Rollout Architecture**

### **5.1 Sequencing Philosophy: Consistency Over Ease of Construction**

The sequence in which the six architectural areas—Admin and Warehouse, Content Pool, Placement, Learning Path, Surviving Readers, and Learner User Interface—ship is governed by one non-negotiable invariant: at no point may a learner see two different answers to the question of their proficiency level on the same day (Questions 11, 12, 13, and 14\)3. Sequencing by what is easiest to build—for instance, shipping the rebuilt Placement engine first while leaving the Learning Path, Goal Feasibility, and Dashboard reading legacy CertificateBands, or shipping the rebuilt Learning Path against the legacy 116-item bank—violates this invariant immediately3.  
To guarantee zero split-brain days, the transition applies the Expand–Contract (Parallel Change)8, Branch by Abstraction11, and Keystone Interface14 patterns adapted for a pre-production environment with a single-file database schema (schema.sql) and acceptable maintenance downtime (Decision T8)3. During the Expand and Seed Dark stages (Phases 1 through 3), the engineering team builds and ships the Staff Warehouse (S-01..S-10), the Automated Gate 1–4 ingestion pipeline, the 456-unit Demo Set and 1,120-unit MVR Production Content Pool, and the dark-launched Placement, Path, and Surviving Reader backend services prior to altering the live learner experience1. During the Atomic Keystone Cutover stage (Phase 4), the pre-production environment enters a scheduled two-hour maintenance window, exports preserved tables (Users, CreditLedger, MentorBookings, and legacy\_v1 ExamAttempts), applies the unified schema.sql to a fresh database instance, loads the validated MVR and Demo content pools alongside preserved records, and activates the rebuilt Placement, Path, Surviving Readers, and Learner UI simultaneously3. Because every writer and every reader switches within the same maintenance window, learners experience zero split-brain days3. Finally, during the Expand Pool and Contract Legacy Code stages (Phases 5 and 6), architects re-publish verified Mock Exam blueprints (S-09), expand the warehouse from MVR (1,120 units) to the Full Production Pool (2,120 units), and delete all legacy placement, path, and fallback code paths once Phase 4 and Phase 5 verification gates pass (Decision T7)1.

### **5.3 Verification Evidence, Smoke Checks, Consistency Definition, and Phase 6 Exit Criteria**

Evaluating when a step is safe to ship beyond unit tests passing (Question 27\) requires four empirical verification artefacts that test concurrency, psychometric discrimination, copy sanitization, and financial conservation1. First, a Concurrency Race-Condition Proof dispatches 50 concurrent placement and four-skill mock exam submissions where Speaking and Writing AI grading callbacks return simultaneously within \< 5ms of each other and out of order, asserting zero PostgreSQL constraint violations, zero deadlocks, and zero orphaned 'in\_progress' snapshots once FreeResponses finish grading2. Second, a Gate 3 and Gate 4 Psychometric Proof exports staging audit telemetry from S-02 and S-08 proving that 100% of active objective items passed dual-model blind solving (![][image152]) and stimulus-blind ablation (![][image153]), 100% of active strata cleared the 10% human SME audit with zero answer-key errors, and both Speaking and Writing rubrics achieved strict monotonicity (![][image154] with ![][image146]) while scoring the Verbose B1 Boilerplate Trap ![][image147]1. Third, an Enum Sanitization Proof (DisplayLabelRegistry Audit) crawls DOM snapshots across every learner screen (SCR-SH-01 through SCR-PR-01) and every surviving reader view across all five certificates, asserting zero occurrences of raw database strings (below\_A1, CAT\_B1, SW\_B2, cannot\_judge, not\_measured, expanded\_remedial) and zero occurrences of % attached to band\_position5. Fourth, a Ledger Conservation Proof runs before and after the Phase 4 cutover import to verify that every user's CreditLedger row count, historical transaction\_reason strings, and net credit balance match the pre-cutover database snapshot byte-for-byte3.  
To prove the product works end-to-end after Phase 4 cutover and Phase 5 mock exam activation (Question 28), an automated smoke-check suite executes two comprehensive user journeys covering a learner who has never taken a placement and a learner mid-path2:

Under this formal definition, first, all six surfaces that answer a learner's current skill level (Dashboard SCR-DB-01, Placement/Standing view SCR-PL-04, Learning Path Header SCR-LP-01, Goal Feasibility starting vector, AI Insight prompt context, and Mentor Booking payload) read the exact same row LearnerSkillState(user\_id, certificate\_code, skill) and return the identical (discrete\_cefr, band\_position) tuple on the same day2. Fifth, the mastery\_probability and mastery\_band shown for (skill, topic\_id, cefr\_level) in Weakness Analysis equals the exact value read by the Learning Path step sizer in LearnerTopicCapability3. Sixth, for every user ![][image165], any cached wallet balance equals ![][image166] and zero debit rows exist for placement, path steps, free drills, or failed-AI retries2.  
Finally, before the legacy placement, static four-week path, and legacy reader branches are permanently deleted from the repository in Phase 6 (Question 14, Decision T7)3, seven quantitative exit criteria must hold true simultaneously in telemetry: zero active LearningPaths, PlacementTests, or in\_progress ExamAttempts reference legacy tables or scoring\_model\_version \= 'legacy\_v1'2; at least 100 complete four-skill placement and mock exam sittings (including simulated AI timeouts and retries) have executed through PlacementSnapshotProjector, ExamAttemptScoringProjector, and StepClosureWriter with zero constraint violations or TWO\_WRITER\_VIOLATION trigger alerts2; the automated assertProductConsistency(u, c) check has run across all active user accounts across all five certificates with zero discrepancies3; all 120 warehouse cells hold at least MVR active stock (1,120 units \+ 120 lessons) with \< 2% of active items quarantined by live telemetry (S-10)1; live productive grading telemetry confirms inter-rater agreement against benchmark anchors of ![][image167] and mean score bias within ![][image168] standardized units (S-08, S-10)1; client error telemetry records zero fallback hits in DisplayLabelRegistry (Rule COPY-01)5; and the immutable pre-Phase-4 database backup snapshot is checksum-verified in cold archive storage3.

## **6\. Data Disposition Table and The Preservation Rule**

### **6.1 The Single Disposition Rule**

Because the platform has no incremental database migration framework and applies a single declarative SQL file (schema.sql) to a fresh database instance (§2.6), preserving any table requires exporting its rows prior to wiping the database, transforming them to match the new schema if necessary, and re-importing them into the fresh database, whereas dropping a table is free3. Rather than making ad-hoc per-table choices, a single architectural rule governs the disposition of every table in the system (Question 22\)3:  
**Rule RULE-DISP-01 (The Canonical Fact-vs-Derivation Disposition Rule):**  
*Preserve (via export-and-import into the fresh database) any table that records an immutable financial ledger entry, user identity or entitlement, active human mentor booking, or a completed, self-contained historical mock exam sitting whose score remains valid on its native certificate scale (scoring\_model\_version \= 'legacy\_v1'); DROP and start clean on any table whose rows are uncalibrated content artefacts (DifficultyLevel 1–5, unlevelled lessons, 12-empty-topic categories) or derived proficiency and curriculum state (PlacementTests, TopicMastery, LearningPaths, cached AiInsights) computed from those defective inputs.*1

### **6.2 Exhaustive Table-by-Table Data Disposition Matrix**

Applying RULE-DISP-01 yields the definitive disposition for every table holding a band, a level, a content unit, or a derived learner record (Questions 18, 19, 20, and 21\)1:

Exported before DB wipe and imported verbatim into CreditLedger with all historical transaction\_reason strings preserved intact3. |
| **Users & UserEntitlements** *(Identity & Subscriptions)* | Learner and staff accounts, authentication credentials, wallet balances, and active certificate selection5. | **PRESERVE & AUGMENT** (Export \-\> Import \+ Default Columns) | **Primary Fact:** Preserved 100%, adding \`account\_mode \= 'production' |

## **7\. The Single-Writer Guarantee and Two-Writer Defect Audit**

### **7.1 Audit of All Seven Two-Writer Defects Across the Transition Seam**

Section 2.7 and Question 25 of the brief highlight one confirmed production-blocking defect—a placement test containing free responses cannot be completed because the attempt stays submitted with a NULL band while a second writer tries to mark PlacementTests as done with a NULL band—and require identifying every other instance of this defect class across the surviving readers of Section 2.22. A comprehensive audit of the nine surviving readers and their interactions with the rebuilt engines reveals six additional two-writer defects (seven in total) that will occur unless prevented by a structural single-writer architecture2:

### **7.2 The Universal Single-Writer Rule and Ownership Matrix**

To eliminate this entire class of defects both during and after the transition (Questions 23 and 25), the platform enforces Rule RULE-SW-01 (Single Authoritative Projector and Strict Read-Source Consolidation)2. Under this rule, every derived snapshot or state table in the database is mutated by **exactly one idempotent service class** executing inside a transaction that acquires a pessimistic SELECT ... FOR UPDATE lock on the authoritative parent record2. No controller, background worker, or user interface endpoint may ever issue a direct INSERT or UPDATE to a derived table; workers mutate only their raw execution row (such as FreeResponses) and invoke the designated projector2.  
Furthermore, to guarantee that no two screens ever disagree on a learner's proficiency level on the same day (Defect 3), PlacementSkillResults is treated strictly as the immutable historical record of that specific placement sitting, whereas LearnerSkillState(user\_id, certificate\_code, skill)—written exclusively by SkillStateProjector whenever Placement finishes, a mock\_section completes, or a learner confirms a Calibration adjustment—serves as the **sole authoritative read table for the learner's current proficiency standing** across Dashboard (SCR-DB-01), Learning Path (SCR-LP-01), Goal Feasibility (FeasibilityCalculator), AI Insight (AiInsight), Weakness Analysis (FR-WEAK-01), Calibration (CalibrationDetector), and Mentor Booking (FR-MENT-01)2. Similarly, to resolve Defect 5, StepClosureWriter is the sole writer for PathSteps.status (in\_progress \-\> closed) and PathWeeks.free\_drill\_unlocked4. When AiGradingCallbackWorker finishes grading a productive practice step asynchronously, it never mutates PathSteps or re-opens a closed week; it writes the rubric scores to FreeResponses and invokes CapabilityUpdateWriter, which updates StepExecutionRecords.improvement\_status, LearnerTopicCapability, and LearnerSkillState.criterion\_profile. If improvement\_status \== 'no\_improvement', the E2 repeat step is queued into the next open slot in the active or buffered window (![][image158] if open steps remain, else ![][image159]) via PathWindowSynthesizer4.

### **7.3 Write-Time Invariant Assertions That Fail Loudly**

Evaluating what invariant can be asserted at write time so a two-writer bug fails loudly rather than silently at read time—and whether the existing placement constraint generalizes (Question 24)—demonstrates that the database constraint that caught the legacy placement bug (status \= 'done' \=\> band IS NOT NULL) generalizes directly into a three-part Write-Time Database Assertion Pattern (RULE-SW-02) enforced across every derived table in schema.sql2.  
First, Algebraic Terminal-State Completeness Constraints (CHECK constraints) ensure that no row can transition to a terminal state ('done', 'graded', 'closed', 'measured') while any asynchronous child dependency remains unresolved or while required output columns are NULL2. Second, a Single-Writer Caller Identity Trigger (enforce\_single\_writer\_identity()) requires every derived table to include a non-nullable column writer\_service\_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL and requires the database transaction to set a transaction-local session variable (SET LOCAL app.current\_writer\_service \= '\<ServiceName\>') before executing an INSERT or UPDATE. A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger verifies current\_setting('app.current\_writer\_service', true) \= NEW.writer\_service\_id AND NEW.writer\_service\_id \= TG\_ARGV\[0\], aborting any unauthorized write immediately with RAISE EXCEPTION 'TWO\_WRITER\_VIOLATION'3. Third, Monotonic Projection Sequence Versioning (projection\_version BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1\) enforces NEW.projection\_version \= OLD.projection\_version \+ 1 via an optimistic concurrency check inside the FOR UPDATE lock so out-of-order worker callbacks cannot overwrite a newer projection2.

| Derived Table | Enforced Write-Time SQL CHECK & Trigger Invariant in schema.sql (Answering Q24) | Exact Class of Two-Writer / Race Bug Caught Loudly at Write Time |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **PlacementTests** | CHECK (status \!= 'done' OR (pending\_grading\_skill\_count \= 0 AND (overall\_cefr IS NOT NULL OR completion\_failure\_reason \= 'all\_examined\_skills\_unmeasured'))) \+ writer\_service\_id \= 'PlacementSnapshotProjector'2 | Catches any code path trying to mark a placement 'done' while productive tasks are still 'pending\_ai' or without resolving overall\_cefr / completion\_failure\_reason (Defect 1\)2. |
| **PlacementSkillResults** | CHECK ((skill\_status NOT IN ('measured', 'reused\_from\_prior') OR (cefr\_level IS NOT NULL AND band\_position BETWEEN 0 AND 100 AND continuous\_theta\_cefr BETWEEN 0.00 AND 6.99)) AND (skill\_status \!= 'not\_measured' OR (cefr\_level IS NULL AND unmeasured\_reason IS NOT NULL)))2 | Prevents writing a measured skill without a valid CEFR band and 0–100 position, or leaving a failed skill with a silent NULL status2. |
| **ExamAttempts** *(Mock Exams)* | CHECK (status \!= 'graded' OR (pending\_free\_response\_count \= 0 AND scaled\_score IS NOT NULL AND certificate\_band\_code IS NOT NULL)) \+ writer\_service\_id \= 'ExamAttemptScoringProjector'2 | Prevents the synchronous Mock Exam controller from marking a 4-skill or TOEIC\_SW mock 'graded' before Speaking and Writing AI workers finish (Defect 2\)3. |
| **LearnerSkillState** | CHECK (discrete\_cefr IS NOT NULL AND band\_position BETWEEN 0 AND 100 AND continuous\_theta \= (cefr\_index(discrete\_cefr) \+ (band\_position::numeric / 100.0))) \+ writer\_service\_id \= 'SkillStateProjector'2 | Guarantees mathematical identity between (discrete\_cefr, band\_position) and continuous\_theta, and blocks rogue controllers from mutating a learner's level outside SkillStateProjector (Defect 3\)3. |
| **LearnerTopicCapability** | CHECK (observations\_count \>= correct\_count AND mastery\_probability BETWEEN 0.000 AND 1.000 AND (mastery\_band \!= 'mastered' OR (mastery\_probability \>= 0.800 AND observations\_count \>= min\_obs\_for\_skill(skill)))) \+ writer\_service\_id \= 'CapabilityUpdateWriter'4 | Prevents any path or drill handler from marking a topic 'mastered' without meeting the minimum observation count (![][image171] objective / ![][image68] productive) and ![][image172] posterior probability (Defect 4\)4. |
| **StepExecutionRecords** | CHECK (improvement\_status NOT IN ('improved', 'no\_improvement') OR (pre\_mastery\_prob IS NOT NULL AND post\_mastery\_prob IS NOT NULL))4 | Prevents closing an objective or graded productive execution record without recording both pre- and post-step capability probabilities (Decision E1, Defect 5\)4. |
| **CreditLedger** | BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger raising LEDGER\_IMMUTABLE\_VIOLATION \+ CHECK (amount \>= 0 OR source\_action\_type IN ('mock\_exam\_sitting', 'standalone\_paid\_ai\_eval'))2 | Enforces append-only immutability (Decision T5) and makes it impossible for placement, path practice, free drills, or failed-AI retries to insert a negative debit row (Defect 7\)2. |

## **8\. Content Readiness Gates**

### **8.1 Minimum Content Thresholds Before Placement, Path, and Mock Exams Launch**

Taking the volume tables of the Content Specification (1.md §6) as given and reconciling them with the placement and path consumption arithmetic (2.md §5.3 and 3.md §5.3) establishes four sequential Content Readiness Gates (Gate C-0 through Gate C-3)1:

### **8.2 Operating Strategy While Content Is Thin**

Determining how the product operates while content is thin—whether via partial rollout to one certificate, a restricted level range, or waiting until the pool reaches full depth (Question 16)—requires evaluating how each option interacts with the shared warehouse architecture (Decision C3: *"One pool, all certificates"*)1. Restricting the launch to a single four-skill certificate (such as IELTS alone) saves zero warehouse items because items are authored and stored by (skill, cefr\_level, topic\_id) rather than by certificate; a single four-skill certificate still requires all four skills (Listening, Reading, Speaking, Writing), all six CEFR bands (A1..C2), and all 20 topics (120 cells)1. Similarly, launching with a restricted level range (such as A2–B2 only) is psychometrically invalid because omitting A1 and C1–C2 items reproduces the exact defect of the legacy 24-question diagnostic, which held zero items at level 5 and misclassified C1 learners as B22.  
Consequently, the platform enforces a strategy of **Full 120-Cell Breadth at MVR Depth (1,120 Units \+ 120 Lessons), Coupled with the 4-Tier Substitution Cascade and Optional Modality-Scoped Phasing**1. Rather than shipping any empty cell in the ![][image173] matrix, Phase 4 launches as soon as all 120 cells reach MVR depth (Gate C-1/C-2: 1,120 assessment units and 120 core lessons), which requires 53% of the authoring volume of the 2,120-unit Full Pool while delivering 100% topic and band coverage across A1..C21. During the interval between Phase 4 (MVR) and Phase 5 (Full 2,120 Pool), if an intensive learner exhausts the 10 to 15 MVR items in a single cell, the Path Engine's Four-Tier Substitution Cascade (BR-POOL-01) seamlessly substitutes unseen items from the closest cognitive sibling topic at the exact same CEFR level (Tier 2\) or adjacent level (Tier 3\) while displaying an explicit disclosure banner (Decision P6: *"when content is missing, substitute and say so"*)4. Furthermore, if the objective Listening and Reading MVR pools (960 items \+ 72 lessons) clear Gates 1–3 and the 10% SME audit ahead of the productive Speaking and Writing MVR pools (160 tasks \+ 48 lessons, which require Gate 4 rubric calibration and three benchmark anchors per task in S-07 and S-08), the architecture supports a clean modality-scoped contingency: activating TOEIC\_CAT (which examines exclusively Listening and Reading per Decision D4) first against the 960 L+R MVR items, while keeping four-skill certificates and TOEIC\_SW gated until the 160 Speaking and Writing tasks and ![][image2] rubrics clear Gate 41. Full-length Mock Exams remain individually gated in S-09 until their section blueprints satisfy INV-1..INV-66.

### **8.3 Content Versioning and Non-Destructive Batch Withdrawal**

To guarantee that a defective content batch can be withdrawn instantaneously without breaking learner history, exam review screens, or capability records that reference it (Question 17), the warehouse enforces a Five-Layer Non-Destructive Content Versioning model1. First, every row in StimulusGroups, ObjectiveItems, ProductiveTasks, Lessons, and Rubrics uses a composite immutable primary key (id, version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1), and foreign keys from AttemptItemResponses, FreeResponses, StepExecutionRecords, and SavedQuestions reference (item\_id, version) with ON DELETE RESTRICT so hard deletion is blocked at the database engine level for any record that has ever left draft state1. Second, once an item version (version \= 1\) has accrued ![][image174] learner attempt, in-place mutation of its stimulus text, audio file, stem, options, correct\_option, or item\_level is blocked in S-05; repairing the item forks a new copy-on-write row (item\_id, version \= 2, lifecycle\_status \= 'draft'), and promoting version \= 2 to 'active' atomically transitions (item\_id, version \= 1\) to 'retired' or 'retired\_defective'1.  
Third, every ingested JSON batch carries an indexed batch\_tag (such as batch\_2026\_11\_r\_b2)1. If post-deployment telemetry (S-10) or SME auditing reveals systemic defects in a batch, executing UPDATE ObjectiveItems SET lifecycle\_status \= 'quarantined' WHERE batch\_tag \= :batch\_tag (and 'retired\_defective' upon confirmation) removes 100% of that batch from all future placement, practice, and dynamic mock selection queries (WHERE lifecycle\_status \= 'active') in under 10 milliseconds without breaking a single historical foreign key1. Fourth, if an item marked retired\_defective was pinned inside a structurally locked Mock Exam (Edition v1, which has ![][image174] completed learner attempt), Edition v1 is never mutated in place (Decision A4); instead, the warehouse automatically forks the mock exam into Edition v2 (supersedes\_edition \= 1), swaps the defective item with an active isomorph from the identical (skill, topic\_id, cefr\_level, question\_type, domain\_context) cell, verifies INV-1..INV-6, and publishes Edition v2 for all future test-takers while historical attempts remain permanently pinned to Edition v16. Fifth, whenever an item or task transitions to retired\_defective, the background MonotonicRecalculationWorker scans all historical ExamAttempts and StepExecutionRecords that administered (item\_id, version) and recomputes each affected session excluding the defective item from the denominator (or crediting the true key): if the recalculation upgrades a learner's LearnerSkillState band or position or flips a LearnerTopicCapability cell to mastered, the upgrade is applied automatically, whereas no learner's level, score, or mastery status is ever downgraded due to a platform content defect1.

## **10\. Theoretical Foundations and Source Alignment on Score Reporting, Crosswalk Caution, and Migration Sequencing**

### **10.1 Psychometric Score Linking Hierarchy and Crosswalk Caution**

In educational measurement, connecting scores across different assessment instruments is governed by the formal taxonomy of score linking established by Holland and Dorans (2006), Dorans, Pommerich, and Holland (2007) in *Linking and Aligning Scores and Scales*, Dorans (2004) in *Applied Measurement in Education*, and Kolen and Brennan (2014) in *Test Equating, Scaling, and Linking*16. Holland and Dorans (2006) demonstrate that score linkages form a strict hierarchy descending from Equating—the strongest statistical claim, requiring two tests to measure the exact same construct with equal reliability, symmetry, equity, and population invariance so scores can be used interchangeably—down through Calibration (measuring the same construct with different reliability or test length), Moderation and Concordance (linking similar constructs measured under different test specifications, such as ACT and SAT), and Projection or Scale Alignment (asymmetric or panel-based cut-score mapping across distinct frameworks)16.  
Applying the Holland and Dorans (2006) framework explains why Decision T2 (*"A band is not a CEFR level"*3) is a foundational psychometric requirement rather than a pedantic naming preference. First, equating is impossible across these instruments because they violate the Equal Construct, Equal Reliability, and Symmetry requirements: the platform's 60-minute two-stage adaptive placement sitting measures general communicative proficiency across A1–C2 (36–40 objective items and 4 productive tasks, achieving dependability ![][image177]2), whereas a TOEIC Listening and Reading mock exam measures workplace receptive comprehension across 200 items (10–990, capping at C1), an IELTS mock measures academic and general mobility (0.0–9.0 up to C2), and a VSTEP.3-5 mock measures national standardized proficiency (0.0–10.0, certifying B1–C1)1. Treating a certificate band as interchangeable with a CEFR level violates the Equity and Population Invariance requirements of equating codified by Kolen and Brennan (2014) and Dorans (2004)16.  
Second, published standard-setting studies establish that certificate-to-CEFR alignments are section-specific minimum cut scores rather than total-score identities1. In ETS's foundational standard-setting study, Tannenbaum and Wylie (2008) (*Mapping the TOEIC and TOEIC Bridge Tests on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages*, ETS Research Report RR-08-34) convened a 22-expert panel using a modified Angoff and construct-congruence procedure to establish independent minimum per-skill cut scores: Listening requires 60 for A1, 110 for A2, 275 for B1, 400 for B2, and 490 for C1, whereas Reading requires 60 for A1, 115 for A2, 275 for B1, 385 for B2, and 455 for C1, Speaking requires 50, 90, 120, 160, 180, and Writing requires 30, 70, 120, 150, 1801. Tannenbaum and Wylie (2008) explicitly refused to map the combined 10–990 TOEIC total score to CEFR bands, because compensatory summing allows a candidate with Listening 450 (above the 400 B2 cut) and Reading 335 (50 points below the 385 B2 cut) to achieve a 785 total while failing the B2 reading construct1. By enforcing per-skill CEFR projection (BR-SEM-02), capping TOEIC and VSTEP projections at C1 in accordance with Ministry of Education and Training of Vietnam Decision 729/QĐ-BGDĐT (2015) and Ton Nu My Nhat (2021)1, reserving C2 (8.5–9.0) exclusively for IELTS on the certificate axis per Lim, Geranpayeh, Khalifa, and Buckendahl (2013)1, and reporting cannot\_judge on non-CEFR band codes (CAT\_B\*, SW\_B\*, Decision T33), this specification aligns every reader with empirical standard-setting literature.

### **10.2 Score Reporting Validity and Non-Compensatory Subscore Profiles**

The visual and textual separation rules in Sections 3 and 4 operationalize the score-reporting validity standards of the *AERA/APA/NCME Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing* (Standard 3.1) as synthesized by Hambleton and Zenisky (2013, 2026\) (*Reporting Test Scores in More Meaningful Ways*), Sinharay, Puhan, Haberman, and Hambleton (2019) (subscore communication versus composite averaging), and Zenisky, Keller, and Park (2019) alongside Kannan, Zapata-Rivera, and Bryant (2021) (preventing vertical-scale misinterpretation)5. Sinharay et al. (2019) and the Council of Europe (2020) *CEFR Companion Volume* establish that averaging distinct communicative modalities—receptive listening and reading versus productive speaking and writing—conceals jagged learner profiles1. Reporting overall\_cefr strictly as the weakest measured skill while initializing each skill's learning path track at its own ![][image18] (BR-SEM-01, BR-SEM-04) ensures that the headline readiness badge reflects the true bottleneck while the curriculum respects each modality's actual standing2. Simultaneously, Zenisky et al. (2019) and Kannan et al. (2021) demonstrate that when a continuous growth scale is partitioned into discrete vertical bands with a within-band index (![][image178]), lay users misinterpret a transition from the top of a lower band (B2 · 78\) to the bottom of a higher band (C1 · 12\) as a regression when the index is formatted as a standalone percentage5. Prohibiting % on band\_position, rendering the six-segment stepped horizon track, and enforcing the \[TĂNG BẬC: B2 (78/100) → C1 (12/100)\] rule across both user interface components and AI insight generators eliminates this cognitive trap2.

### **10.3 Evolutionary Database Design, Branch by Abstraction, and Keystone Cutovers**

The rollout sequence in Section 5 and the single-writer architecture in Section 7 operationalize three foundational patterns from continuous delivery and evolutionary software architecture: Expand–Contract (Parallel Change) formalized by Fowler and Sadalage (2006) in *Refactoring Databases* and Fowler (2014)8, Branch by Abstraction established by Fowler (2014) and Hammant (2013)11, and the Keystone Interface pattern described by Fowler (2020)14. When migrating a domain concept whose semantics and grain have changed—from a single scalar CertificateBands reference to a four-skill LearnerSkillState vector and a 120-cell LearnerTopicCapability matrix—Fowler and Sadalage establish that the new schema and writers must be expanded and verified in parallel before contracting legacy readers8. Because this platform applies a single declarative schema.sql file to a fresh database without incremental migration scripts (§2.6) and operates pre-production where a maintenance window is acceptable (Decision T8)3, Phases 1 through 3 execute the Expand phase in dark staging mode, Phase 4 executes the Migrate phase via a deterministic two-hour export-import cutover window, and Phase 6 executes the Contract phase by deleting the legacy code paths once verification telemetry is green (Decision T7)3. Rather than developing the five rebuilt subsystems on long-lived source-control branches that drift semantically from the nine surviving readers12, Branch by Abstraction routes all reader queries through the consolidated domain interfaces (LearnerSkillState, LearnerTopicCapability, ExamAttemptScoringProjector)11, while the Keystone Interface switch (USE\_CEFR\_UNIFIED\_MODEL) holds back the learner-facing transition until Content Readiness Gates C-1 and C-2 (1,120 MVR assessment units and 120 levelled core lessons) and all nine surviving readers are verified together1.
